findings.text: File lock classification uses distinct low single bit positions starting at zero to distinguish POSIX style, BSD style, delegation, access probe, existence probe, lease, close release, blocking wait, downgrade pending, unlock pending, open file description ownership, layout, reclaim, and three directory delegation ignore cases for create delete and rename. A combined close value merges POSIX and close bits.

Deferred lock indicator is a small integer constant. Lease break requests use low single bit positions distinguishing full lease plus delegation breaks, delegation only, layout only, nonblocking request, read only open trigger, and directory delegation triggers for create delete and rename.
Permission check mask uses low bits for execute, write, read, append, access, open and chdir, plus a separate nonblocking modifier bit that constrains the check to not sleep.

Open file mode uses single bit positions across low and middle bits to record read, write, seekability, pread, pwrite, exec, restricted write, atomic write capability, two hash width variants, no ctime update, random hint, metadata presence, path only, atomic position, writer accounting, readable, writable, opened, created, stream, direct capability, no reuse, backing file, two notify suppression variants, nowait, unmount need and no accounting. A combined mask merges the two notify suppression bits.

Attribute update mask uses low single bit positions to select mode, owner, group, size, access time, modification time, change time, explicit time sets, force, change time set, set-user-id kill, set-group-id kill, file reference, privilege kill, open truncate, times set, touch and delegation preservation. Whiteout mode and device are both zero.

IO control block flags reuse read write flag values for priority, data sync, sync, nowait, append, atomic, cache bypass and signal suppression, and add higher single bit positions for eventfd completion, direct path, write direction, page wait queue, no IO, cache allocation, async read write state and metadata presence. A tracing table maps each flag to a short human label.

Page cache tags alias generic index marks zero through two for dirty, writeback and to-write states. Inode operation flags use low bits for fast permission, lookup, nofollow, extended attribute, default link target, mtime management, cached link, fast exec permission and lock context presence. Access control cache uses two distinct negative pointer sentinels for not cached and do not cache. Positive address operation returns use large values above normal range for writepage activation and truncated page. Stack depth limit is two.

Common lock core holds a pointer to the blocker when waiting, linkage into per inode context, membership in global lists, a list of blocked waiters plus membership linkage for queueing on a blocker, owner identity, flag word, small type code, process identifier, CPU index for global list placement, wait queue and owning file reference.

Range lock embeds the common core, adds start and end offsets, two callback table pointers for filesystem private handling and lock manager handling, and a filesystem specific variant area covering network state, version four state, distributed filesystem pending queue linkage with grant state and debug identity, and clustered filesystem inode reference. Field layout is randomized.

Lease embeds the common core, adds async notification linkage, two deadline values for break and downgrade handling, and a lease manager callback table, with randomized layout. Per inode lock context holds a spinlock guarding three separate lists for BSD style, POSIX style and leases.

Filesystem lock callbacks provide copy and release-private hooks. Lock manager callbacks provide module owner reference, owner lookup and release, unblock notification, grant decision, expirability test and expiry action. Lease manager callbacks provide break decision, parameter change, setup, breaker ownership test, open conflict check and timeout test. Manager registry holds list linkage and a flag showing whether opens block during grace.

Attribute update request carries a validity mask, mode, dual representations for owner and group supporting both classic identifiers and idmap aware wrappers with identical values, size, three timestamps for access modification and change, and an optional file reference meaningful only when the file bit is set in the mask.

IO control block carries file reference, current offset, completion callback, private pointer, flag word, IO priority, write stream hint and an optional page wait queue valid only when the wait queue flag is set. Address space carries host inode, page index, invalidation semaphore, allocation mask, writable mapping counter, interval tree root, page count, writeback index, operation table pointer, flag word, writeback error sequence, private spinlock and mapping semaphore with long alignment and randomized layout. Buffer metadata helper carries owning mapping pointer, guarding spinlock and buffer list.

Address space operation table offers hooks for reading a folio, writing back pages, dirtying, readahead, beginning and ending writes, block mapping probe, folio invalidation, release, freeing, direct IO, migration, laundering, partial uptodate check, dirty writeback query, error removal and swap activation plus deactivation.
Module exposes a read write flag type alias and two callback type aliases for block mapping from inode plus block index and for direct IO completion from control block plus offset.

In locking enabled builds read and write predicates test the small type code inside the core against read and write lock values; in disabled builds both predicates are constant false and wakeup is a no operation.

Asynchronous locking is considered possible when the file operation table lacks a lock hook or advertises async capability through its flag word. Wakeup in enabled builds delegates to a waiter wake helper acting on the core.
Iteration helper walks entries of a context list using the core list linkage. Mapped test reports true when the interval tree root inside the address space is non empty.

Writable mapping accounting uses an atomic counter where positive means writably mapped. Mapping increments only from non negative, unmapping decrements, denying decrements only from positive, and allowing increments. Deny fails when already denied and map fails when already write denied.

Per inode lock context spinlock guards its three lock lists. Address space invalidation semaphore orders truncation against page operations, private spinlock guards private data, and mapping semaphore guards the interval tree; helpers provide nonblocking try acquire for read and write plus debug assertions for held and held for write states. Buffer metadata list has its own spinlock.

When locking support is absent, query operations report invalid argument, set operations report access or invalid errors, lease query reports unlocked, and delegation operations report invalid argument.

Without locking support, context release, lock and lease initialization, conflock and lock copy, POSIX and file removal, POSIX test, block deletion, test and cancel helpers are no operations with fixed success or not-found results, while locking attempts report missing lock support and inode-has-locks and blocker checks report false; lease time fetch is empty and lease establish or modify report invalid argument.

Layout break helper in enabled builds orders memory, looks up the inode lock context, and only when a non empty lease list exists requests a layout break with an optional nonblocking modifier; otherwise it reports success. Disabled builds always report success without inspection. Delegation inode wrapper holds an inode pointer when enabled and is empty otherwise.

Lease lifecycle includes stable held plus downgrade pending and unlock pending transitional marks, with reclaim origin and ignore hints for directory delegation events. Blocked requests queue on the blocker core through member linkage and are woken through the core wait queue; unblock notification and grant hooks drive progress, and a blocking mark distinguishes waiting requests.

Disabled locking configuration silently drops enforcement: type predicates are always false, listings are empty, removal and cancellation claim success, and set paths fail with fixed errors, so callers cannot distinguish absent support from contention without checking build configuration.
